correctness.rationale: For odd N at least three, centering the finite Markov matrix yields a product of a symmetric circulant and a permutation. Equality in its mean-zero norm bound forces a permutation eigenvector in the first Fourier plane. Nonreal modes give rotations, fixed modes give independent reflection-pair swaps, and the odd cosine moment forces sign-reversing modes to arise from a full reflection. Their overlaps give N*2^((N-1)/2). The boundary locations apply to finite matrices for all odd N and to the BV transfer spectrum only for N>=5. For N=3 the identity shuffle has an additional transfer eigenvalue at the essential radius, exhibited by the three-cycle jump function in RESULT.md. The included finite-matrix checker corroborates but does not prove the infinite theorem.
residual_risks: Floating-point matrix checks do not establish exact equality or probe the transfer spectrum at the essential radius.
